### Purpose Statement

This playbook answers the twelve core engineering questions that every team faces when working with APIs in the enterprise. It applies to all products and platforms — not only AWS deployments — and covers both internal service APIs (East-West traffic) and external-facing APIs (North-South traffic). Platform-specific implementation is addressed through referenced implementation artifacts. This playbook, and the AWS-specific artifacts it references (GUID-APP-IMPL-009, REF-APP-API-001, STD-APP-API-007, STD-APP-MON-002, GUID-APP-IMPL-011), are currently draft and pending Domain EA and Security Architecture review.

[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-010-api-engineering-guidance.md#business-value]

### Business Value

- Provides a single, consolidated set of intended answers to recurring API engineering questions, pending Domain EA and Security Architecture review.
- Reduces per-team re-design of governance, inventory, versioning, and protection models.
- Ensures internal and external APIs are treated consistently and with appropriate controls.
- Cross-references the complete EA artifact set so teams can start from EA artifacts as they are approved, rather than ad-hoc decisions.

[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-010-api-engineering-guidance.md#q1-how-do-i-inventory-my-apis]

### Q1: How Do I Inventory My APIs?

**Answer:** Publish a contract in the specification format appropriate to the API style — OpenAPI 3.x for REST, `.proto` for gRPC, GraphQL SDL for GraphQL, or an AsyncAPI/schema-registry contract for event-driven APIs (see [Q11](#q11-is-openapi-the-standard)) — for every API, internal and external, and register it in the enterprise API catalog.
page_texts.21:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-010-api-engineering-guidance.md#what-an-api-inventory-contains]

#### What an API Inventory Contains

An API inventory is the authoritative registry of every API the organization owns. Each entry in the catalog records:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| API ID | Unique identifier (e.g., service name + major version) |
| API Type | Internal (East-West) or External (North-South); see [STD-APP-API-003](../../../../standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-003-internal-external-api-guidelines.md) |
| Traffic Pattern | North-South or East-West; see [STD-APP-API-004](../../../../standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-004-north-south-east-west-apis.md) |
| Owner | Domain and team |
| API Specification | Link to the versioned contract (OpenAPI, `.proto`, GraphQL SDL, or AsyncAPI) in source control |
| Lifecycle Stage | Design / Active / Deprecated / Retired |
| Consumer Registry | Known consumers (internal services or external clients) |
| Classification | Data sensitivity and regulatory classification |
page_texts.22:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-010-api-engineering-guidance.md#inventory-process]

#### Inventory Process

1. **Create the API specification** in the format appropriate to the API style during API design — OpenAPI 3.x for REST (contract-first per [STD-APP-API-001](../../../../standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-001-api-design.md)); `.proto`, GraphQL SDL, or AsyncAPI/schema-registry for non-REST styles (see [Q11](#q11-is-openapi-the-standard)).
2. **Commit the spec to source control** in the owning service repository.
3. **Register the API** in the enterprise developer portal or API catalog when the API is promoted to a shared or production environment.
4. **Update the catalog** at each major lifecycle transition: deprecation, version change, or retirement.
5. **Audit the catalog periodically** to identify undocumented or orphaned APIs.
page_texts.23:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-010-api-engineering-guidance.md#internal-api-inventory]

#### Internal API Inventory

Internal APIs (East-West) should be inventoried with the same discipline as external APIs. The catalog entry for an internal API includes the consumer services, the trust model (mTLS, service tokens), and the service mesh policy if applicable.

> **Key principle:** An API that is not in the catalog does not have an owner, does not have known consumers, and cannot be governed, deprecated, or secured systematically. Internal APIs are not exempt.

[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-010-api-engineering-guidance.md#tooling]

For AWS deployments, see [REF-APP-API-001](../../../../strategy/reference/application/REF-APP-API-001-aws-api-management-reference-architecture.md) for the API Management platform that supports catalog publishing.

[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-010-api-engineering-guidance.md#q2-how-do-i-version-my-apis]

### Q2: How Do I Version My APIs?

**Answer:** Use URL path versioning (`/v1/`, `/v2/`) for external APIs. Follow the versioning and deprecation patterns in [PTN-APP-API-020](../../../../patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-020-api-versioning-pattern.md) and [PTN-APP-API-009](../../../../patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-009-api-deprecation-pattern.md).
page_texts.26:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-010-api-engineering-guidance.md#versioning-rules]

#### Versioning Rules

- **Major version in the URL path**: `/api/v1/`, `/api/v2/`. Increment only for breaking changes.
- **Minor and patch versions** are backward-compatible and do not require a URL path change.
- **Never remove a version without completing the deprecation lifecycle** defined in [PTN-APP-API-009](../../../../patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-009-api-deprecation-pattern.md).
- **Backward compatibility is mandatory** for external APIs during the deprecation window. Internal APIs may coordinate breaking changes through team agreement but must still follow the lifecycle pattern.
page_texts.27:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-010-api-engineering-guidance.md#versioning-by-api-type]

#### Versioning by API Type

| API Type | Versioning Approach | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| External (North-South) | URL path versioning; strict backward compatibility | Consumers cannot be forced to upgrade |
| Internal (East-West) | URL path versioning or coordinated contract bump | Coordinated deployment possible; still follow lifecycle |
| Async/Event (internal or external) | Schema versioning in message metadata | See [PTN-APP-API-024](../../../../patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-024-event-driven-architecture-pattern.md) |
page_texts.28:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-010-api-engineering-guidance.md#deprecation-lifecycle]

#### Deprecation Lifecycle

1. Announce the deprecation with a planned sunset date (minimum notice period per consumer agreement).
2. Update the style-appropriate contract (OpenAPI `deprecated: true` for REST; equivalent deprecation marker otherwise — see [Q11](#q11-is-openapi-the-standard)).
3. Return a `Deprecation` header in responses during the deprecation window.
4. Monitor consumer traffic to confirm migration before retiring.
5. Remove the version only after all known consumers have migrated.

---

### Q3: How Do I Publish My API for Use?

**Answer:** The publication path depends on who consumes the API.
page_texts.30:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-010-api-engineering-guidance.md#publication-paths-by-consumer-type]

#### Publication Paths by Consumer Type

| Consumer | Publication Path | Tooling |
| --- | --- | --- |
| External (public internet) | API Gateway → Developer Portal with OAuth/API key onboarding | [REF-APP-API-001](../../../../strategy/reference/application/REF-APP-API-001-aws-api-management-reference-architecture.md), [PTN-APP-API-023](../../../../patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-023-self-service-developer-portal-pattern.md) |
| Partner (B2B) | API Gateway → Scoped developer portal or direct provisioning with partner-specific tokens | [STD-APP-API-003](../../../../standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-003-internal-external-api-guidelines.md) |
| Internal services (East-West) | Private API Gateway (mandatory baseline on AWS; platform-neutral gateway/mesh per STD-APP-API-006 elsewhere) → service registry or internal catalog, with service mesh policy as a complementary layer | [Q8](#q8-does-api-management-apply-to-east-west-or-only-north-south), [STD-APP-API-006](../../../../standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-006-api-mesh-vs-gateway-guidance.md), [PTN-APP-API-031](../../../../patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-031-service-mesh-integration-pattern.md) |
page_texts.31:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-010-api-engineering-guidance.md#publication-checklist]

#### Publication Checklist

Before publishing any API to consumers:

- [ ] A style-appropriate API contract (OpenAPI for REST; `.proto`, GraphQL SDL, or AsyncAPI otherwise — see [Q11](#q11-is-openapi-the-standard)) is authored, reviewed, and committed to source control.
- [ ] API is classified (internal/external, North-South/East-West).
- [ ] Authentication and authorization controls are configured (see [Q4](#q4-how-do-i-protect-my-api)).
- [ ] API is registered in the appropriate catalog (developer portal for external; service registry for internal).
- [ ] Observability is configured per [Q12](#q12-how-do-i-observe-my-apis).
- [ ] Lifecycle stage is set to Active in the catalog.
- [ ] Consumer onboarding documentation is published alongside the spec.
page_texts.32:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-010-api-engineering-guidance.md#api-gateway-vs-direct-exposure]

#### API Gateway vs Direct Exposure

All North-South APIs must be published through an API Gateway. Do not expose backend service endpoints directly to external consumers. East-West APIs on AWS are also published through a Private API Gateway as the mandatory control-plane baseline (see [Q8](#q8-does-api-management-apply-to-east-west-or-only-north-south)); on non-AWS platforms, on-premises, or for native gRPC/event APIs Amazon API Gateway cannot proxy, apply the platform-neutral gateway/mesh decision framework in [STD-APP-API-006](../../../../standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-006-api-mesh-vs-gateway-guidance.md) instead. Where a gateway applies, service mesh policy layers mTLS and traffic control on top of that baseline — it does not substitute for gateway publication.

[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-010-api-engineering-guidance.md#q4-how-do-i-protect-my-api]

### Q4: How Do I Protect My API?

**Answer:** Security controls differ for North-South (external-facing) and East-West (internal) APIs. Both require explicit protection.
page_texts.34:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-010-api-engineering-guidance.md#north-south-external-api-protection]

#### North-South (External) API Protection

| Control | Requirement | Reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TLS | TLS 1.2 minimum, TLS 1.3 preferred, at the gateway | [STD-APP-API-005](../../../../standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-005-api-gateway-management.md) |
| Authentication | OAuth 2.0 / OIDC for user-facing; for M2M, use cryptographically bound credentials (mTLS client certificates or OAuth 2.0 client-credentials/workload-identity tokens) per [GUID-SEC-IAM-NON-HUMAN-AND-AI-STRATEGY-2.2.12](../../../../strategy/guidance/security/Identity/GUID-SEC-IAM-NON-HUMAN-AND-AI-STRATEGY-2.2.12.md) — API keys alone identify the calling application for metering/throttling (see [GUID-APP-IMPL-011](./GUID-APP-IMPL-011-aws-api-management-platform-guidance.md)) and are not sufficient M2M authentication | Security guidance (see below) |
| Authorization | Token-based RBAC/ABAC at the gateway or service layer | [STD-APP-API-005](../../../../standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-005-api-gateway-management.md) |
| Rate Limiting / Throttling | Per-client rate limits enforced at the gateway | [STD-APP-API-005](../../../../standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-005-api-gateway-management.md) |
| WAF | Layer-7 protections (OWASP Top 10, bot protection) | Security guidance |
| Input Validation | Validate all inputs against the style-appropriate API contract schema (OpenAPI for REST; see [Q11](#q11-is-openapi-the-standard) for other styles) | [PTN-APP-API-019](../../../../patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-019-input-validation-pattern.md) |
| Audit Logging | Capture all access and policy decisions | Security guidance |

For the full API security controls baseline, refer to:
- [GUID-SEC-APP-API-SECURITY-2.7.01](../../../../strategy/guidance/security/Application/GUID-SEC-APP-API-SECURITY-2.7.01.md)
- [GUID-SEC-INT-API GATEWAY-2.8.01](../../../../strategy/guidance/security/integration-security/GUID-SEC-INT-API%20GATEWAY-2.8.01.md)
- [GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-APIGW-2.7.11](../../../../strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-APIGW-2.7.11.md)
page_texts.35:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-010-api-engineering-guidance.md#east-west-internal-api-protection]

#### East-West (Internal) API Protection

Internal APIs must not be treated as implicitly trusted. Apply zero-trust principles even within the service boundary:

| Control | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| Gateway Interception | Private API Gateway (mandatory baseline on AWS; platform-neutral gateway/mesh per STD-APP-API-006 elsewhere) intercepts East-West calls per [Q8](#q8-does-api-management-apply-to-east-west-or-only-north-south) |
| Service Identity | Mutual TLS (mTLS) between services; certificates managed by service mesh or cert manager |
| Token-based Authorization | Service-to-service tokens with scoped permissions; validate at the receiving service |
| Network Policy | Restrict which services may call which endpoints using gateway policy plus mesh policies or Kubernetes NetworkPolicy |
| Audit Logging | Log service-to-service calls at the gateway, mesh, or sidecar layer |

Refer to [PTN-APP-API-004](../../../../patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-004-service-communication-pattern.md) for service communication security patterns and [STD-APP-API-004](../../../../standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-004-north-south-east-west-apis.md) for East-West security requirements.
page_texts.36:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-010-api-engineering-guidance.md#healthcare--phi-considerations]

#### Healthcare / PHI Considerations

APIs handling Protected Health Information (PHI) require additional controls. Review [GUID-SEC-APP-API-SECURITY-2.7.01](../../../../strategy/guidance/security/Application/GUID-SEC-APP-API-SECURITY-2.7.01.md) for HIPAA-aligned API security guidance before designing APIs that process or transmit PHI.

### Q5: What Infrastructure Services Do I Need?

**Answer:** The infrastructure needed depends on whether the API is North-South (external) or East-West (internal), and on the deployment platform.
page_texts.38:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-010-api-engineering-guidance.md#north-south-externalpartner-facing-apis]

#### North-South (External/Partner-Facing) APIs

| Capability | Required Component | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| API Ingress | API Gateway | Managed (e.g., Amazon API Gateway, Kong, NGINX) or self-managed |
| Identity / AuthN | Identity Provider (IdP) with OIDC/OAuth2 | Enterprise IdP federation |
| Threat Protection | WAF + DDoS mitigation | Placed at the API gateway perimeter |
| Developer Enablement | Developer Portal | API catalog, onboarding, and documentation hosting |
| Lifecycle Management | CI/CD with contract and policy validation | Prevents unreviewed changes from reaching production |
| Observability | OTel Collector → enterprise backends (Kubernetes/EKS, proposed pending STD-APP-MON-002 ratification); CloudWatch/X-Ray for Lambda/ECS | See [Q12](#q12-how-do-i-observe-my-apis) |

For AWS-specific service mappings, see [REF-APP-API-001](../../../../strategy/reference/application/REF-APP-API-001-aws-api-management-reference-architecture.md) and [STD-APP-API-007](../../../../standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-007-aws-api-management-standard-profile.md).
page_texts.39:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-010-api-engineering-guidance.md#east-west-internal-service-to-service-apis]

#### East-West (Internal Service-to-Service) APIs

| Capability | Required Component | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| API Ingress (control-plane baseline) | Private API Gateway | Mandatory baseline per [GUID-SEC-NETWORK-API-GW-AWS-2.2.04.SSB](../../../../strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-NETWORK-API-GW-AWS-2.2.04.SSB.md) on AWS (endpoint type `PRIVATE`, VPC Endpoint-only); see [Q8](#q8-does-api-management-apply-to-east-west-or-only-north-south) |
| Service Discovery | Service registry or DNS-based discovery | Kubernetes service DNS, Consul, etc. |
| mTLS | Service mesh control plane | Currently, [PTN-APP-API-031](../../../../patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-031-service-mesh-integration-pattern.md) (`status: active`) permits **Istio or Linkerd** as the mesh implementation. Sidecar proxy differs by mesh: Istio uses **Envoy** as its sidecar; Linkerd uses its own Rust-based **`linkerd2-proxy`** sidecar (lighter-weight than Envoy — see PTN-APP-API-031's Linkerd variation) — the two are not interchangeable and this distinction affects resource sizing, policy capabilities, and troubleshooting guidance. [STD-INFRA-EKS-001](../../../../standards/infrastructure/eks/STD-INFRA-EKS-001-eks-auto-mode-container-compute.md) REQ-EKS-007b (currently `status: draft`) proposes narrowing the approved set to **Istio** only (with AWS App Mesh, EOL 2026-09-30, no longer viable) once ratified — until that ratification, mesh selection continues to defer to the active PTN-APP-API-031 pattern, and Linkerd remains permitted; complementary to the Private API Gateway baseline, not a substitute for it |
| Traffic Policies | Mesh policy engine or Kubernetes NetworkPolicy | Circuit breaking, retries, timeouts |
| Observability | OTel instrumentation + service mesh metrics (Kubernetes/EKS, proposed pending STD-APP-MON-002 ratification); CloudWatch/X-Ray for Lambda/ECS | See [Q12](#q12-how-do-i-observe-my-apis) |
| Internal Catalog | Service registry or internal portal | Keeps internal API consumers discoverable |

See [Q8](#q8-does-api-management-apply-to-east-west-or-only-north-south) for the Private API Gateway baseline requirement and [PTN-APP-API-031](../../../../patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-031-service-mesh-integration-pattern.md) for service mesh infrastructure guidance.

[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-010-api-engineering-guidance.md#when-both-are-needed]

#### When Both are Needed

Most non-trivial services have both North-South ingress (for external or partner consumers) and East-West communication (to upstream internal services). Deploy both layers with appropriate controls. The API Gateway handles the N-S boundary. For the E-W boundary on AWS, the API Gateway also intercepts it — per the mandatory Private API Gateway baseline in [Q8](#q8-does-api-management-apply-to-east-west-or-only-north-south) — with the service mesh layering mTLS and traffic policy on top of that baseline within the cluster or VPC. On non-AWS platforms, on-premises, or for native gRPC/event APIs Amazon API Gateway cannot proxy, apply the platform-neutral gateway/mesh decision in [STD-APP-API-006](../../../../standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-006-api-mesh-vs-gateway-guidance.md) for the E-W boundary instead.

### Q6: How Does an Engineering Team Configure These?

**Answer:** Follow the phased implementation approach in [GUID-APP-IMPL-009](./GUID-APP-IMPL-009-aws-api-management-implementation-guidance.md) for AWS deployments. The generic process for any platform is:

[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-010-api-engineering-guidance.md#configuration-steps-platform-agnostic]

#### Configuration Steps (Platform-Agnostic)

**Phase 1: API Design and Classification**

1. Author the style-appropriate API contract before writing implementation code (contract-first) — OpenAPI 3.x for REST; see [Q11](#q11-is-openapi-the-standard) for other styles.
2. Classify the API: internal vs external ([STD-APP-API-003](../../../../standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-003-internal-external-api-guidelines.md)), North-South vs East-West ([STD-APP-API-004](../../../../standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-004-north-south-east-west-apis.md)).
3. Select the appropriate management and protection pattern based on [Q9](#q9-when-do-i-use-api-management-vs-service-mesh).
4. Register the API in the inventory ([Q1](#q1-how-do-i-inventory-my-apis)).

**Phase 2: Infrastructure and Controls**

5. Provision the API gateway or service mesh components appropriate to the traffic pattern.
6. Configure authentication, authorization, and rate-limiting policies at the gateway or mesh layer.
7. Integrate WAF and threat protection for North-South APIs.
8. For Kubernetes/EKS-deployed services, configure OTel instrumentation in the service code per [STD-APP-MON-002](../../../../standards/application/monitoring/STD-APP-MON-002-opentelemetry-observability.md), once that standard completes ratification (currently `status: draft`); other platforms follow their applicable observability baseline (see [Q12](#q12-how-do-i-observe-my-apis)).

**Phase 3: Publish and Validate**

9. Validate API contracts and policies in CI/CD before promotion.
10. Publish to the developer portal (external) or internal service registry (internal).
11. Validate observability: confirm traces, metrics, and logs are flowing to enterprise backends.
12. Complete a pre-production readiness checklist including security control evidence.

**Phase 4: Operate and Evolve**

13. Monitor API health using the enterprise observability platform.
14. Apply versioning and deprecation lifecycle management per [Q2](#q2-how-do-i-version-my-apis).
15. Run periodic API inventory audits.

For AWS-specific step-by-step guidance, see [GUID-APP-IMPL-009](./GUID-APP-IMPL-009-aws-api-management-implementation-guidance.md). For the AWS service configuration profile, see [STD-APP-API-007](../../../../standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-007-aws-api-management-standard-profile.md).

**Answer:** The **recommended** enterprise API operating model is **federated delivery with centralized shared controls**. This is a Recommended-tier practice, not a mandated operating model: per [STD-APP-API-007](../../../../standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-007-aws-api-management-standard-profile.md) Practice 9, no ratified standard or accepted ADR currently authorizes this model as a Constraint, and teams should not treat it as an enforceable requirement until one does.

#### What This Would Mean in Practice, If Adopted

- Domain teams **would not** need to build their own gateway infrastructure from scratch; they would consume shared platform components.
- Domain teams **would** own their API contracts, versioning decisions, and consumer onboarding documentation.
- Shared controls (WAF, IdP, OTel Collector (Kubernetes/EKS workloads; proposed pending STD-APP-MON-002 ratification), policy templates) would be changed by the platform team through governed change processes.
- Domain teams would be able to extend configurations within bounds set by shared templates but not relax shared control requirements.

Until an accepted ADR or ratified standard establishes this model, treat the above as recommended practice rather than an enforceable operating model — document any team-level deviation rationale rather than treating conformance as mandatory.

[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-010-api-engineering-guidance.md#implications-for-internal-east-west-apis-under-this-proposed-model]

#### Implications for Internal (East-West) APIs, Under This Proposed Model

If this recommended model is adopted, it would apply to internal APIs as well. On AWS, the mandatory Private API Gateway baseline for REST East-West APIs (see [Q8](#q8-does-api-management-apply-to-east-west-or-only-north-south)) is a control-plane requirement independent of this operating-model question; under the proposed federated model, that gateway and the service mesh policies that govern East-West communication would both be managed by a central platform team — the team that operates the Private API Gateway and the service mesh control plane. On non-AWS platforms, on-premises, or for native gRPC/event APIs where the platform-neutral gateway/mesh choice in [STD-APP-API-006](../../../../standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-006-api-mesh-vs-gateway-guidance.md) applies instead, the equivalent shared infrastructure (gateway and/or mesh control plane, whichever is selected) would likewise be managed centrally under this proposed model. Individual domain teams would configure service-level policies within that shared infrastructure.

### Q8: Does API Management Apply to East-West or Only North-South?

**Answer:** Both, but with different tools and controls.
page_texts.48:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-010-api-engineering-guidance.md#north-south-external-boundary--api-management--api-gateway]

#### North-South (External Boundary) → API Management / API Gateway

- Applies to all APIs exposed outside the service cluster or VPC — to external users, partners, or other organizational units across a security boundary.
- Use an API Management platform (API Gateway + lifecycle management + developer portal).
- Apply external security controls: WAF, rate limiting, OAuth/OIDC, input validation.
- Reference: [STD-APP-API-005](../../../../standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-005-api-gateway-management.md), [REF-APP-API-001](../../../../strategy/reference/application/REF-APP-API-001-aws-api-management-reference-architecture.md).
page_texts.49:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-010-api-engineering-guidance.md#east-west-internal-service-to-service--private-api-gateway-mandatory-baseline-on-aws-for-rest-apis--service-mesh-complementary-or-gatewaymesh-per-std-app-api-006-other-platforms]

#### East-West (Internal Service-to-Service) → Private API Gateway (mandatory baseline on AWS for REST APIs) + Service Mesh (complementary), or Gateway/Mesh per STD-APP-API-006 (other platforms)

- Applies to service-to-service communication within the same cluster, VPC, or trust boundary.
- **On AWS, for East-West traffic implemented as a REST API**, the active security control baseline [GUID-SEC-NETWORK-API-GW-AWS-2.2.04.SSB](../../../../strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-NETWORK-API-GW-AWS-2.2.04.SSB.md) mandates a Private API Gateway (endpoint type `PRIVATE`, VPC Endpoint-only) as the East-West control-plane baseline (REQ-APIGW-01/03/04) — internal traffic on AWS is not exempt from gateway interception. This AWS-specific mandate does not extend to non-AWS clouds, on-premises environments, or native gRPC/event APIs that Amazon API Gateway does not proxy (see below).
- **On AWS, for East-West traffic implemented as an HTTP or WebSocket API**, the `PRIVATE` endpoint type is not available — HTTP and WebSocket APIs support only Regional (internet-routable) endpoints. A VPC Link/NLB integration does **not** satisfy the private-endpoint baseline, since it privatizes only the API Gateway-to-backend integration, not the API's own client-facing endpoint. Per [STD-APP-API-007](../../../../standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-007-aws-api-management-standard-profile.md) Requirement 5 (the authoritative source for this framing), the SBB's control — API Gateway interception plus private, non-internet-routable endpoints — applies to REST, HTTP, and WebSocket APIs alike, with no exception by API type; because no technical mechanism lets an HTTP or WebSocket API satisfy that control, this is a genuine, unresolved SBB/technical-capability gap, not a design choice this guidance (or an implementing team) can resolve on its own authority. No internal Application Load Balancer, other private frontend, or VPC Link/NLB integration is authorized as a sanctioned substitute. Re-platform the boundary as a REST API using the `PRIVATE` endpoint type wherever the API's actual requirements permit it; any East-West HTTP or WebSocket API that cannot be re-platformed as REST is an open compliance gap that must be tracked and remediated through Security Architecture's SBB exception process (or an SBB amendment) rather than resolved through a self-approved workaround.
- **On non-AWS clouds, on-premises environments, or for native gRPC/event APIs (e.g., raw gRPC, Kafka/event-driven APIs) that a REST/HTTP-oriented gateway does not proxy**, no equivalent enterprise-wide gateway-interception mandate currently applies. Apply the platform-neutral decision framework in [STD-APP-API-006](../../../../standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-006-api-mesh-vs-gateway-guidance.md) instead, which permits mesh-only internal communication (no gateway interception layer) where appropriate for the traffic pattern and control requirements.
- Layer a service mesh (Istio or Linkerd, per [PTN-APP-API-031](../../../../patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-031-service-mesh-integration-pattern.md); see also the Istio-narrowing proposal, pending ratification, in [STD-INFRA-EKS-001](../../../../standards/infrastructure/eks/STD-INFRA-EKS-001-eks-auto-mode-container-compute.md) REQ-EKS-007b) on top of the AWS Private API Gateway baseline (where applicable) or as the primary East-West control (on other platforms, per STD-APP-API-006) for mTLS, traffic policies, circuit breaking, and observability between services.
- Reference: [PTN-APP-API-031](../../../../patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-031-service-mesh-integration-pattern.md), [STD-APP-API-004](../../../../standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-004-north-south-east-west-apis.md), [STD-APP-API-006](../../../../standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-006-api-mesh-vs-gateway-guidance.md).

#### Decision Rule

```
Is the consumer outside the service cluster/VPC boundary?
  YES → North-South → API Gateway + API Management
  NO  → East-West:
          Is this AWS, and is the traffic proxyable by Amazon API Gateway?
            YES → Is the API implemented as a REST API?
                    YES → Private API Gateway (mandatory baseline on AWS, endpoint type PRIVATE)
                          + Service Mesh (complementary, optional)
                          — see GUID-SEC-NETWORK-API-GW-AWS-2.2.04.SSB for the AWS-specific control
                    NO  → HTTP or WebSocket API: PRIVATE endpoint type is not available
                          (Regional-only). This is an unresolved SBB/technical-capability
                          gap per STD-APP-API-007 Requirement 5, not a sanctioned
                          alternative: re-platform as REST using PRIVATE wherever the
                          API's actual requirements permit it; otherwise track as an open
                          compliance gap through Security Architecture's SBB exception
                          process. No ALB or other private frontend is authorized as a
                          substitute, and a VPC Link/NLB integration alone does not close
                          the gap either — it privatizes only the gateway-to-backend
                          integration, not the client-facing endpoint.
            NO  → Non-AWS platform, on-premises, or native gRPC/event API not proxyable by Amazon API Gateway
                  → Apply the platform-neutral Gateway vs. Mesh decision framework in STD-APP-API-006
                    (mesh-only internal communication is permitted where appropriate)
```

Note that a single service may have both: a North-South API Gateway endpoint for external consumers, and an East-West control appropriate to its platform (AWS Private API Gateway, optionally paired with mesh; or a platform-neutral gateway/mesh choice per STD-APP-API-006 elsewhere) for calls to upstream internal services.

### Q9: When Do I Use API Management vs Service Mesh?

**Answer:** Use the decision framework in [STD-APP-API-006](../../../../standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-006-api-mesh-vs-gateway-guidance.md). The quick answer is:

| Use Case | Tool | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| External clients, partners, or cross-boundary consumers | API Management (Gateway) | Centralized policy enforcement, consumer onboarding, lifecycle governance |
| Service-to-service within a cluster or VPC, on AWS (proxyable by Amazon API Gateway) | Private API Gateway (mandatory baseline on AWS) + Service Mesh (complementary) | Gateway provides the control-plane interception baseline (see [Q8](#q8-does-api-management-apply-to-east-west-or-only-north-south)); mesh adds distributed mTLS, per-service observability, and traffic resilience on top of it |
| Service-to-service within a cluster or VPC, on non-AWS platforms, on-premises, or for native gRPC/event APIs Amazon API Gateway cannot proxy | Gateway or Mesh per [STD-APP-API-006](../../../../standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-006-api-mesh-vs-gateway-guidance.md) | No AWS-specific gateway-interception mandate applies; apply the platform-neutral decision framework, which permits mesh-only internal communication where appropriate |
| Both (same service has external and internal traffic) | Both boundaries require a North-South gateway; the East-West control follows the applicable branch above (AWS Private API Gateway + mesh, or platform-neutral gateway/mesh per STD-APP-API-006) | Mesh is additive to, not a substitute for, the gateway control-plane baseline where that baseline applies |
| Developer portal, API catalog, subscription management | API Management | Lifecycle and business management features are API Management capabilities, not mesh capabilities |
| mTLS between internal services, circuit breaking, retries | Service Mesh (layered on the AWS Private API Gateway baseline where applicable, or standalone per STD-APP-API-006 elsewhere) | These are mesh primitives that complement the AWS gateway control-plane baseline where mandated, or serve as the primary East-West control where no such mandate applies |
page_texts.52:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-010-api-engineering-guidance.md#why-not-rely-on-service-mesh-alone-for-east-west-aws]

#### Why Not Rely on Service Mesh Alone for East-West? (AWS)

**On AWS**, a service mesh alone distributes mTLS, circuit breaking, and per-service observability efficiently to sidecars co-located with each service, but it does not satisfy the Private API Gateway control-plane baseline mandated by the active AWS security control ([GUID-SEC-NETWORK-API-GW-AWS-2.2.04.SSB](../../../../strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-NETWORK-API-GW-AWS-2.2.04.SSB.md); see [Q8](#q8-does-api-management-apply-to-east-west-or-only-north-south)). Deploy the Private API Gateway as the required interception point for East-West AWS traffic proxyable by Amazon API Gateway, and layer the service mesh on top of it for the resilience and observability primitives it provides. **This mandate is AWS-specific** — on non-AWS platforms, on-premises, or for native gRPC/event APIs Amazon API Gateway cannot proxy, no equivalent enterprise-wide gateway-interception mandate applies, and mesh-only internal communication is permitted per [STD-APP-API-006](../../../../standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-006-api-mesh-vs-gateway-guidance.md).

For the full decision framework and architectural comparison, see [STD-APP-API-006](../../../../standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-006-api-mesh-vs-gateway-guidance.md).

#### OpenAPI Documentation Requirements

An OpenAPI specification published to the developer portal must include:

- `info.title`, `info.version`, `info.description` — must be clear and consumer-facing.
- All operations with `summary`, `description`, and example request/response payloads.
- All response codes — including error codes with `description` and example bodies.
- Security scheme definitions matching the actual authentication mechanism used.
- Deprecation markers (`deprecated: true`) on deprecated operations.
- Lifecycle stage indicated in `info.x-lifecycle-status` or equivalent extension.

[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-010-api-engineering-guidance.md#keeping-documentation-current]

#### Keeping Documentation Current

- **Contract as the source of truth**: Author the contract first (OpenAPI for REST; style-appropriate format otherwise) and generate server stubs and client SDKs from it. Do not generate the published spec from code annotations. If framework annotations are already in use for other reasons, restrict them to drift-checking the implementation against the committed contract — they are not the source of truth for the published spec.
- **Contract validation in CI/CD**: Validate the spec against [STD-APP-API-001](../../../../standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-001-api-design.md) requirements in the pipeline.
- **Developer portal sync**: Automate spec publishing to the developer portal as part of the release pipeline to ensure the published documentation matches the deployed API.

For developer portal configuration and the self-service API onboarding pattern, see [PTN-APP-API-023](../../../../patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-023-self-service-developer-portal-pattern.md) and [PTN-APP-API-010](../../../../patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-010-api-documentation-pattern.md).

[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-010-api-engineering-guidance.md#observability-for-internal-east-west-apis]

#### Observability for Internal (East-West) APIs

On AWS, the Private API Gateway baseline (see [Q8](#q8-does-api-management-apply-to-east-west-or-only-north-south)) emits access logs and metrics for East-West calls in the same manner as it does for North-South traffic. On non-AWS platforms, on-premises, or for native gRPC/event APIs where the platform-neutral gateway/mesh choice in [STD-APP-API-006](../../../../standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-006-api-mesh-vs-gateway-guidance.md) applies instead, the selected gateway or mesh control plane is the equivalent source of access logs and metrics. Service mesh sidecars (Envoy, the Istio sidecar proxy) additionally emit metrics and traces at the network layer. Kubernetes/EKS-deployed application services are expected to further instrument at the code level using OTel per [STD-APP-MON-002](../../../../standards/application/monitoring/STD-APP-MON-002-opentelemetry-observability.md) — proposed, pending that standard's ratification (currently `status: draft`) — to emit semantic spans and custom metrics not available from the gateway or sidecar alone; Lambda/ECS backends outside Kubernetes/EKS scope follow the CloudWatch/X-Ray AWS-native baseline instead. API Gateway itself does not emit OTLP signals to the OTel Collector — its access logs and metrics flow to CloudWatch (and X-Ray for tracing), as described under AWS-Specific Observability below. Configure the OTel Collector as a DaemonSet or sidecar aggregator to receive signals only from application code and service mesh telemetry exporters; correlate gateway-originated CloudWatch/X-Ray telemetry with OTel Collector-routed application telemetry using the propagated trace context (W3C `traceparent`) rather than a shared ingestion path.

[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-010-api-engineering-guidance.md#observability-for-north-south-externalgateway-apis]

#### Observability for North-South (External/Gateway) APIs

The API gateway emits access logs and metrics natively. Configure the gateway to:
- Forward access logs to the enterprise SIEM.
- Emit request metrics (rate, latency, error rate) to the enterprise observability platform.
- Propagate trace context headers (W3C `traceparent`) to backend services so gateway and backend spans are correlated in the OTel trace.

#### AWS-Specific Observability

For teams using AWS, CloudWatch and X-Ray are the gateway-layer observability backends. Application services deployed on Kubernetes/EKS behind the gateway should instrument with OTel per [STD-APP-MON-002](../../../../standards/application/monitoring/STD-APP-MON-002-opentelemetry-observability.md) — proposed, pending that standard's ratification (currently `status: draft`) — and route application-level telemetry through the OTel Collector — not through the AWS X-Ray SDK directly; Lambda/ECS backends outside Kubernetes/EKS scope use the CloudWatch/X-Ray baseline instead.

### Implementation Methodology

Apply the answers in this playbook in sequence during API design:

1. **Classify the API** (Q1, Q8) — determine type, traffic pattern, and consumer model.
2. **Inventory and spec the API** (Q1, Q11) — create the style-appropriate API contract and register the API.

5. **Configure observability** (Q12) — for Kubernetes/EKS-deployed services, OTel instrumentation before production (proposed, pending STD-APP-MON-002 ratification); Lambda/ECS services validate against the CloudWatch/X-Ray baseline instead.
6. **Publish** (Q3) — developer portal for external; internal catalog for internal.
7. **Govern** (Q2, Q7) — versioning, deprecation lifecycle, federated delivery model.

#### Decision Point 1: API Management vs. Service Mesh

**Context:** Selecting the management model for a given API boundary.
**Options:** API Gateway (API Management), Service Mesh, or both.
**Criteria:** Whether the consumer is outside the service cluster/VPC boundary ([Q8](#q8-does-api-management-apply-to-east-west-or-only-north-south)); AWS deployments must additionally satisfy the Private API Gateway baseline required by the active AWS security control baseline (see [GUID-APP-IMPL-009](./GUID-APP-IMPL-009-aws-api-management-implementation-guidance.md) and [REF-APP-API-001](../../../../strategy/reference/application/REF-APP-API-001-aws-api-management-reference-architecture.md) for the AWS-specific decision).
**Recommendation:** Use API Gateway for all North-South traffic. For East-West traffic on AWS, apply the Private API Gateway baseline mandated by the applicable AWS security control, layering service mesh as a complementary control for mTLS and traffic policy where needed; see [STD-APP-API-006](../../../../standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-006-api-mesh-vs-gateway-guidance.md) for the general decision framework.

### Use Case 1: New External REST API (North-South)

An engineering team is building a new FHIR R4 Patient Access API for external consumers.

1. **Classify**: External API, North-South traffic pattern.
2. **Inventory**: Author OpenAPI 3.x spec, commit to source control, register in developer portal.
3. **Management model**: API Management (gateway + developer portal). No service mesh for N-S ingress.
4. **Protection**: OAuth 2.0 / SMART on FHIR at gateway; WAF with OWASP Top 10 ruleset; rate limiting per client; PHI classification applied per [GUID-SEC-APP-API-SECURITY-2.7.01](../../../../strategy/guidance/security/Application/GUID-SEC-APP-API-SECURITY-2.7.01.md).
5. **Observability**: for the FHIR service deployed on Kubernetes/EKS, OTel SDK instrumented per [STD-APP-MON-002](../../../../standards/application/monitoring/STD-APP-MON-002-opentelemetry-observability.md) (proposed, pending ratification); gateway access logs forwarded to SIEM.
6. **Publish**: Spec published to developer portal; onboarding flow guides external consumers.
7. **Govern**: URL path versioning (`/fhir/r4/`); deprecation policy per [PTN-APP-API-009](../../../../patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-009-api-deprecation-pattern.md).

[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-010-api-engineering-guidance.md#use-case-2-internal-microservice-api-east-west]

### Use Case 2: Internal Microservice API (East-West)

An internal Claims Processing service exposes an API consumed by the Eligibility and Payment services within the same Kubernetes cluster.

1. **Classify**: Internal API, East-West traffic pattern.
2. **Inventory**: Author OpenAPI spec for the internal contract; register in internal service registry.
3. **Management model** (AWS): Private API Gateway (mandatory baseline on AWS, per [Q8](#q8-does-api-management-apply-to-east-west-or-only-north-south); platform-neutral gateway/mesh per STD-APP-API-006 on other platforms) with Service Mesh layered on top for mTLS and traffic policies.
4. **Protection**: Private API Gateway interception; mTLS via service mesh; service-to-service token authorization; network policy restricts callers to Eligibility and Payment services only.
5. **Observability**: OTel SDK (per STD-APP-MON-002, proposed pending ratification) in each service and service mesh sidecar metrics feed the enterprise OTel Collector; Private API Gateway access logs and metrics flow to CloudWatch and the enterprise SIEM separately — the gateway does not emit signals into the OTel Collector.
6. **Publish**: Spec and team ownership published to internal catalog.
7. **Govern**: Coordinated contract versioning; consumer teams notified of breaking changes.

[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-010-api-engineering-guidance.md#use-case-3-service-with-both-n-s-and-e-w-traffic]

### Use Case 3: Service with Both N-S and E-W Traffic

A Provider Portal service receives external partner requests (N-S) and calls an internal Credential Verification service (E-W).

- **N-S path**: Partner request → API Gateway (WAF + OAuth + rate limit) → Provider Portal service.
- **E-W path** (AWS): Provider Portal service → Private API Gateway (mandatory baseline on AWS) + Service Mesh (mTLS + circuit breaker) → Credential Verification service. On non-AWS platforms, on-premises, or for native gRPC/event APIs Amazon API Gateway cannot proxy, apply the platform-neutral gateway/mesh choice per [STD-APP-API-006](../../../../standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-006-api-mesh-vs-gateway-guidance.md) for this leg instead.
- Both paths require observability configuration: gateway access logs for N-S; for services deployed on Kubernetes/EKS, Private API Gateway access logs + OTel traces (per STD-APP-MON-002, proposed pending ratification) + mesh metrics for E-W.
